title: Token Corridor Competitive Decision-Control Plane
mission: Define and prove a provider-neutral bounded-decision control plane (working name Token Corridor) inside the AgentSwitchboard software factory: compile messy repository/runtime evidence into typed decision requests, select the cheapest adequate judgment engine, preserve calibrated uncertainty and authority provenance, compose decisions with deterministic code, and route execution without duplicating Jev, Prompt Kit, FirstMate, or AgentSwitchboard execution adapters.

owner.role: Competitive architecture and bounded decision protocol owner

wave: Competitive architecture → decision protocol → measured factory integration
safeParallelWork: Existing Triage→ASB live-dispatch plan may continue; this plan consumes its receipts but does not rewrite its dispatcher.
Execution-adapter trio work may continue; Token Corridor selects or recommends an engine/route but does not replace execution adapters.
Prompt Kit P143/P55/P07 convergence work may continue in web-excel-repair-triage; Prompt Kit remains semantic/workflow policy authority.
FirstMate crew/runtime work may continue; FirstMate remains canonical live crew/session runtime.
NodeWeaver can be evaluated read-only as a future semantic-signal provider without expanding its production scope.
ownedScope: Competitive reference architecture and product-boundary plan under plans/active/
Future provider-neutral bounded-decision request/receipt contract and engine interface under a dedicated AgentSwitchboard decision-corridor surface if TC-01 is admitted
Decision-engine calibration, abstain/escalate, cost/latency, provenance, and authority-separation contracts
Factory decision benchmark/evaluation fixtures and receipts
A thin AgentSwitchboard factory-router vertical slice that consumes Prompt Kit/ASB evidence and uses bounded judgments only where deterministic rules are insufficient
NodeWeaver role evaluation as an optional signal/provider, not automatic expansion
Standalone Token Corridor extraction gate after multi-consumer/runtime evidence
forbiddenScope: Training or cloning a Jev-class foundation/system-one model as the near-term competitive response
Creating a standalone TokenCorridor repository before the extraction gate is satisfied
Building a second FirstMate-style crew/session scheduler
Replacing Prompt Kit semantic/workflow policy ownership or P95 Evidence Spine continuation ownership
Allowing a probabilistic model to mint permission, authorization, merge authority, destructive authority, or deployment authority
Treating typed output as semantic correctness or calibrated confidence as proof of authorization
Expanding stale NodeWeaver roadmap claims without a refreshed benchmark/prototype
Copying external source code without a separate provenance/license/security adoption decision
expectedArtifacts: Source-backed Jev/software-factory reference matrix with ADOPT/ADAPT/REJECT/UNKNOWN dispositions
Token Corridor product-boundary contract: decision plane vs Prompt Kit policy vs ASB execution vs FirstMate crew runtime vs NodeWeaver semantic signals
Provider-neutral decision-request and decision-receipt contract with stable action/state fingerprints
DecisionModel-like adapter interface with deterministic baseline and structured-model/Jev-compatible adapter seams
Authority invariant: probabilistic engines may classify/recommend/block/escalate but cannot create authorization
Calibration/evaluation corpus for factory decisions with accuracy, calibration, latency, cost, false-autonomy, and unnecessary-escalation measures
First end-to-end vertical slice for factory routing/recovery using existing ASB execution and Prompt Kit evidence owners
Standalone-repository extraction decision based on at least two real consumers or a proven independent deployment/runtime boundary

tasks.title: Freeze competitive reference baseline and local product boundaries
inputs: TypeSafe Jev official launch material dated 2026-09-15
outputs: Reference-pattern disposition ledger and solved-baseline/gap map
acceptanceCriteria: Jev is classified as an external bounded-decision primitive rather than the software-factory product boundary.
SWE-AF/AgentFactory are classified as direct factory-control references.
OpenHands scheduling/runtime ownership split and Pydantic durable-resume patterns are captured separately.
Local owners are explicit: Prompt Kit policy/semantics; Token Corridor decision control; AgentSwitchboard execution control; FirstMate live crew; NodeWeaver optional semantic signal layer.
Claims are evidence-typed and external marketing is not promoted to local runtime proof.

tasks.title: Build the bounded-decision protocol floor
inputs: Prompt Kit Evidence Spine continuation and authority semantics
Jevwire DecisionModel/advisory-only patterns as external reference
outputs: Structured-model/Jev-compatible adapter seam without required live credential
Negative fixtures proving a model cannot mint authorization
acceptanceCriteria: Decision state/evidence, action authority, and execution state are mechanically separate.
Request binds a stable state/action fingerprint and expected typed question shape.
Receipt records engine identity/version, probability/confidence, calibration provenance when available, latency/cost when observable, disposition, and proof ceiling.
Unknown/low-confidence paths abstain or escalate instead of fabricating certainty.
Authorization originates only from typed upstream grant/policy/owner evidence; no model output can create it.
Interface allows Jev, open/local System-One-style engines, structured LLMs, and deterministic code without changing downstream factory contracts.

tasks.title: Build the competitive decision benchmark
inputs: Real sanitized factory decision families: route, retry/replan/split/escalate, next-owner, evidence sufficiency, model/runtime tier
At least one structured generative-model baseline
Jev-compatible backend when credentials/runtime are available
acceptanceCriteria: Measure task accuracy/agreement against reviewed labels.
Measure calibration with Brier score and/or ECE where probability semantics permit.
Measure p50/p95 latency and observable cost.
Measure false autonomous-action rate and unnecessary-escalation rate.
Do not claim Jev superiority or infer local moat until the same corpus is evaluated across backends.
Benchmark can run without Jev credentials using local/deterministic baselines.

tasks.title: Ship one factory-router vertical slice
outputs: One end-to-end bounded factory routing path with receipts
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic rules run before any probabilistic engine.
A bounded probabilistic decision is used only where semantic judgment remains.
The chosen ADW/execution route is passed to existing ASB execution ownership rather than executed by Token Corridor itself.
Blocked/user-only authority gates remain durable and resumable.
The same scenario can be replayed with deterministic, structured-model, and Jev-compatible decision backends without changing the workflow contract.

tasks.title: Insert cheap judgment into adaptive factory control loops
outputs: Bounded decision points for retry vs replan vs split vs escalate and next-owner selection
acceptanceCriteria: Do not duplicate FirstMate crew scheduling.
Deterministic validator failures route directly when ownership is known.
Probabilistic judgment is reserved for ambiguous failure classification or strategy selection.
Every decision produces a receipt linked to the execution/proof artifact it influenced.
Expensive agent calls are avoided when deterministic or lower-cost decision engines meet the benchmarked confidence/risk policy.

tasks.title: Close durable AFK continuation across judgment and execution
outputs: Crash/restart-resumable transition proof across decision → dispatch → receipt → continuation
acceptanceCriteria: A process interruption does not require the operator to reconstruct or repaste the workflow.
Stable transition/request identity prevents duplicate execution after retry.
External/user-only gates quiesce durably and resume when the gate changes.
Scheduler, decision plane, execution runtime, and evidence sink have distinct owners.
Observed end-to-end proof distinguishes planned/dispatched/executed/validated states.

tasks.title: Decide NodeWeaver's role by prototype evidence
outputs: KEEP/NARROW/ADAPT/RETIRE decision for NodeWeaver in the factory
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh NodeWeaver implementation truth instead of relying on its 2025 gap analysis.
Prototype NodeWeaver only as a semantic feature/signal provider unless evidence proves a stronger unique role.
Compare its useful signals against simpler embeddings/rules and the decision backends in TC-02.
Do not expand weighted-node/topic-emergence roadmap merely to compete with Jev.
Record whether NodeWeaver supplies unique recurrence/topic/state features that materially improve factory decisions.

tasks.title: Apply standalone Token Corridor extraction gate
inputs: At least one measured factory consumer
acceptanceCriteria: Do not create a standalone repository merely because the working name exists.
Extraction requires at least two real consumers OR a proven independent deployment/runtime/release boundary with clear ownership benefit.
P143 Repository Convergence Planner is used if extraction requires moving capabilities from multiple donor repositories.
A standalone repo must have a stable contract, independent validation/release need, and no duplicate ASB/Prompt Kit/FirstMate authority.

validation: For TC-01+: run the focused decision-corridor contract/tests plus the automated test floor before integration.
For TC-02+: retain benchmark receipts tied to exact engine/version/config and corpus revision.
For TC-05: require observed runtime receipt; static contracts cannot promote to AFK runtime proof.

proof.target: Durable competitive architecture plan narrowing Jev/software-factory precedent into an executable AgentSwitchboard product seam.
proof.achieved: Reference research completed and local current heads reconciled: ASB d90e5ed457c0657b6016c3ead0c976bf679a8de1; NodeWeaver add0fd24cb213afdad4cb082db9ba8af947cc228; Prompt Kit/Triage c97718247e7b14544d198035dd3cdc07725545a8. Plan is proposed; decision protocol/runtime not implemented by this planning lane.
proof.ceiling: This plan proves a source-backed architectural/product factoring decision only. It does not prove Jev quality on the user's workload, Token Corridor runtime behavior, NodeWeaver value to the factory, live autonomous dispatch, cost savings, or a standalone product/repository boundary.

Keep Token Corridor as a working name until TC-07.
Jev is a candidate backend/reference primitive, not the product boundary.
The first implementation invariant is that probabilistic judgment cannot mint authorization.
